meta.title: Octa Pass: everything sensitive, in one place only you can open
meta.description: Octa Pass keeps everything sensitive in one end-to-end encrypted vault: passwords, passkeys and one-time codes, and also SSH keys, API secrets, .env files, cards, IDs, Wi-Fi, crypto wallets and encrypted folders. Free, synced to every device, no ads. Open source, so anyone can check it.

site.footer: Octa Pass is a free, encrypted home for everything sensitive, funded by donations, sponsors and grants. No ads. No trackers. Its code is open source under the MIT License.

hero.title: Everything sensitive, in one place only you can open.
hero.sub: Passwords and passkeys, yes. And SSH keys, API secrets, cards, IDs, Wi-Fi, crypto wallets and whole folders of files. Synced to every device, encrypted so only you can read them. Free, with no ads.
hero.status: Public alpha: sign-ups are open in the web vault. The apps are coming to the stores.
hero.titleRest: in one place only you can open.

everything.lede: If losing it would hurt, or someone reading it would, it belongs here. Every kind of item is encrypted on your device the same way, syncs the same way and shares the same way.
everything.filterLabel: Show what Octa Pass keeps for

groups.label: Everything
groups.blurb: 22 kinds of secret, one master password, one Secret Key, one place to look.

groups.label: Everyday
groups.blurb: Logins, passkeys and codes, plus the Wi-Fi password, the recovery codes and the note you’d never put in a notes app.

groups.label: Money
groups.blurb: Cards and bank accounts with payment QR codes, software licences, and crypto wallets whose seed phrase is never shown as a QR code.

groups.label: Identity
groups.blurb: Passports, driver’s licences and national IDs with their scans, and the identities and addresses that fill sign-up forms.

groups.label: Developers
groups.blurb: SSH keys with an agent, API keys, OAuth tokens, .env files, database logins and certificates, kept out of your repo and your shell history.

groups.label: Files
groups.blurb: Documents with any item, Safes that lock whole folders with your vault, and files encrypted for you or anyone else.

statement.lead: Everything in your vault is encrypted on your device before it syncs. Here’s one login twice: once as you see it, once as our server keeps it. An SSH key, a passport scan or a .env file looks the same to us.
statement.tabsLabel: Choose a view of the same login
statement.caption: The same login, as you see it and as our server stores it.
statement.captionLive: Real ciphertext, made in your browser just now with a key that was then thrown away. This is all our server would ever hold.

bento.passkeysBody: Create and use passkeys in your browser, and on your phone as its passkey provider. They sync, encrypted, to every device.
bento.fillBody: Only on the exact site a login belongs to, and only when you ask.
bento.breachTitle: Breach checks that never see your password
bento.breachBody: Your device sends only the first 5 characters of a hash, and compares the matches itself.
bento.aliasBody: A different forwarding address for every site, through the alias service you choose.
bento.recoveryBody: See which email and phone can reset each account, and how many backup codes you have left. If one email is compromised, you know exactly what’s at risk.
bento.cardsBody: Checkout and sign-up forms, filled. Nothing is processed, only stored encrypted.
bento.importBody: And leave whenever you want, passkeys included.

points.title: An SSH agent that asks
points.body: Your keys stay in the vault. ssh and git use them through the desktop app, and every signature asks Touch ID, Windows Hello or your password first.

points.title: .env files, without the file
points.body: Keep environments in the vault and hand them to one command with octapass run. Values can point at other items, so a password lives in one place.

points.title: CI that can’t leak your vault
points.body: Service accounts give a pipeline read-only access to one shared vault, with a token our server never sees. There’s a GitHub Action and a GitLab template.

points.title: A toolkit that stays local
points.body: Make certificates and a local CA, sign and read JWTs, hash and encode. Every tool runs on your device.

files.titleLine2: Not just the password to them.
files.lede: A Safe is a folder that locks with your vault. While you’re unlocked it’s a folder like any other. Lock, and every file and every name on disk is ciphertext.
files.locked: Locked. This is what’s on the disk.
points: One key per file. Each file is encrypted on its own, and each change gets a new key.
Names hidden too. On disk a Safe is a flat set of blobs with random names.
Send files to anyone. Encrypt in the open age format for another Octa Pass user, a passphrase or yourself.

features: Unlimited items of every kind: logins, keys, cards, IDs and more
Unlimited devices, synced in real time
Autofill in browsers, on iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows and Linux
An SSH agent and secrets for your scripts
Family sharing for up to 6 people
free.note: Nothing to set up. Create an account in the web vault today, and the apps sync with it as they reach the stores.
free.howTiny: Your vault is tiny. A whole vault of 500 logins, keys and notes is about a megabyte of encrypted data, so hosting it costs very little.
free.howNoAds: No ads, and nothing to sell. We can’t read your vault, so there’s no data to profit from even if we wanted to.
free.howFunded: Funded in the open. Donations, sponsors and grants will pay for the servers, with the costs published every month.

sealed.title: Sealed before it leaves your hands.

steps.title: Two secrets unlock it
steps.body: Your master password, plus a 128-bit Secret Key that lives only on your devices and in your printed Recovery Kit.

steps.title: Your device makes the key
steps.body: Argon2id turns them into your Account Unlock Key. That key never leaves the device.

steps.title: Every item gets its own lock
steps.body: Each item is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under its own random key, sealed by your vault key.

steps.title: Only ciphertext travels
steps.body: Sign-in uses OPAQUE, so your password never crosses the network. Our server only ever holds sealed items.

platforms.title: On every device you own.
platforms.lede: Where the operating system lets a password manager fill passwords, Octa Pass uses it. Where it doesn’t, the browser extension and an auto-type shortcut fill the gap. The web vault is open now; the apps are built and coming to the stores.

open.titleLine2: so you don’t have to trust us.
open.code: Anyone can check the code. The service you use runs the same MIT code that’s published, and it gets an independent security audit before 1.0.

roadmap.title: Built in the open, one phase at a time.

items.q: Is Octa Pass a password manager?
items.a: Yes, and more. It does what you’d expect from a password manager, and keeps the rest of what’s sensitive in the same encrypted vault: SSH keys with an SSH agent, API keys and .env files, certificates, crypto wallets, passports and IDs, Wi-Fi networks, and Safes, folders whose files are encrypted one by one. One master password, one Secret Key, one place to look.
Yes. Unlimited items and devices, family sharing for up to 6 people and 1 GB for files, with no trial period and no ads. It’s funded by donations, sponsors and grants.

items.q: Can you see what I store?
items.a: No. Your vault is encrypted on your device before it syncs, and the keys never reach our server. That goes for every item and every file, not only passwords. A stolen copy of our database would also need your Secret Key, which we never receive.

items.q: What if I forget my master password?
items.a: You recover with the recovery code in your Recovery Kit, or through an emergency contact you set up. We can’t reset it for you. That’s the price of a server that can’t read your data.
Ad code next to your secrets would be a security hole, and an app that holds everything sensitive has to be trusted completely. Octa Pass is funded by donations, sponsors and grants.

Yes, as a public alpha: create a free account in the web vault. The apps are built and coming to the stores. The independent security audit comes before 1.0, so don’t rely on Octa Pass alone for anything important yet.

items.q: Can I run my own server?
items.a: Yes, it’s optional. The server is open source, and the same Octa Pass apps connect to it: choose “Self-hosted” when you sign in and enter your server’s address. Autofill, passkeys and Face ID work the same way.

items.q: Can I bring my passwords from another app?
items.a: Yes. Octa Pass imports from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Bitwarden, 1Password, LastPass, Proton Pass, Dashlane, Keeper, KeePass, authenticator apps and the FIDO Credential Exchange Format. SSH keys come in from ~/.ssh, and .env files from your projects.
